chunks: And from him, from Muhammad, from Ahmad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The raqabah is freed from the mustaḍ'afīn.' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الرَّقَبَةُ: A slave who has entered into a contract of manumission (kitābah) with their master, to be freed upon payment of an agreed sum.
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weak or constrained; here referring to those who have a manumission contract but lack the full means to pay it immediately.

ai.seo_question: Who frees the raqabah slave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'raqabah' slave eligible for manumission is specifically drawn from the 'mustaḍ'afīn', those bound by a *mudabbar* contract or possessing the means to pay. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on prioritizing the liberation of slaves who have actively sought or are capable of securing their freedom through financial means, thereby linking manumission directly to the slave's agency and economic status.
